doc:
If this option is not `none`, the builtin `intros` rule unfolds the goal's
target with the given transparency to discover `∀` binders. For example, with
`def T := ∀ x y : Nat, x = y`, `introsTransparency? := some .default` and goal
`⊢ T`, the `intros` rule produces the goal `x, y : Nat ⊢ x = y`. With
`introsTransparency? := some .reducible`, it produces `⊢ T`. With
`introsTransparency? := none`, it only introduces arguments which are
syntactically bound by `∀` binders, so it also produces `⊢ T`.

def Aesop.Stats.trace (p : Aesop.Stats) (opt : Aesop.TraceOption) : Lean.CoreM Unit

value.text:
fun p opt => do
  let __do_lift ← opt.isEnabled
  if (!__do_lift) = true then pure ()
    else
      match p with
      |
      { total := total, configParsing := configParsing, ruleSetConstruction := ruleSetConstruction,
          search := search, ruleSelection := ruleSelection, script := script,
          forwardState := forwardState, scriptGenerated := scriptGenerated, ruleStats := ruleStats,
          goalStats := _goalStats } =>
        have totalRuleApplications := Array.foldl (fun total rp => total + rp.elapsed) 0 ruleStats;
        do
        Lean.addTrace opt.traceClass
            (Lean.toMessageData "Total: " ++ Lean.toMessageData total.printAsMillis)
        Lean.addTrace opt.traceClass
            (Lean.toMessageData "Configuration parsing: " ++
              Lean.toMessageData configParsing.printAsMillis)
        Lean.addTrace opt.traceClass
            (Lean.toMessageData "Rule set construction: " ++
              Lean.toMessageData ruleSetConstruction.printAsMillis)
        Lean.addTrace opt.traceClass
            (Lean.toMessageData "Script generation: " ++ Lean.toMessageData script.printAsMillis)
        Lean.addTrace opt.traceClass
            (Lean.toMessageData "Script generated: " ++
              Lean.toMessageData
                (match scriptGenerated with
                | none => (Lean.MessageData.ofFormat ∘ Std.format) "no"
                | some g => (Lean.MessageData.ofFormat ∘ Std.format) g.toString))
        Aesop.withConstAesopTraceNode opt
            (pure (Lean.toMessageData "Search: " ++ Lean.toMessageData search.printAsMillis))
            (do
              Lean.addTrace opt.traceClass
                  (Lean.toMessageData "Rule selection: " ++
                    Lean.toMessageData ruleSelection.printAsMillis)
              Lean.addTrace opt.traceClass
                  (Lean.toMessageData "Forward state updates: " ++
                    Lean.toMessageData forwardState.printAsMillis)
              Aesop.withConstAesopTraceNode opt
                  (pure
                    (Lean.toMessageData "Rule applications: " ++
                        Lean.toMessageData totalRuleApplications.printAsMillis ++
                      Lean.toMessageData " [total / successful / failed]"))
                  (have timings := Aesop.sortRuleStatsTotals p.ruleStatsTotals.toArray;
                  do
                  forIn timings PUnit.unit fun x __s =>
                      match x with
                      | (n, t) => do
                        Lean.addTrace opt.traceClass
                            (Lean.toMessageData "[" ++
                                                      Lean.toMessageData
                                                        (t.numSuccessful + t.numFailed) ++
                                                    Lean.toMessageData " " ++
                                                  Lean.toMessageData
                                                    (t.elapsedSuccessful +
                                                        t.elapsedFailed).printAsMillis ++
                                                Lean.toMessageData " / " ++
                                              Lean.toMessageData t.numSuccessful ++
                                            Lean.toMessageData " " ++
                                          Lean.toMessageData t.elapsedSuccessful.printAsMillis ++
                                        Lean.toMessageData " / " ++
                                      Lean.toMessageData t.numFailed ++
                                    Lean.toMessageData " " ++
                                  Lean.toMessageData t.elapsedFailed.printAsMillis ++
                                Lean.toMessageData "] " ++
                              Lean.toMessageData n)
                        pure (ForInStep.yield PUnit.unit)
                  pure ())
                  false)
            false

fun rule subst =>
  Lean.Meta.withNewMCtxDepth do
    let __do_lift ← Lean.instantiateMVars rule
    let lmvarIds : Array Lean.LMVarId := (Lean.collectLevelMVars { } __do_lift).result
    forIn' [:lmvarIds.size] PUnit.unit fun i h __s =>
        match Aesop.Substitution.findLevel? { toNat := i } subst with
        | some l => do
          Lean.assignLevelMVar lmvarIds[i] l
          pure (ForInStep.yield PUnit.unit)
        | x => pure (ForInStep.yield PUnit.unit)
    let __do_lift ← Lean.Meta.inferType rule
    Lean.Meta.forallTelescopeReducing __do_lift fun fvarIds x =>
        have args := Array.mkEmpty fvarIds.size;
        have remainingFVarIds := Array.mkEmpty fvarIds.size;
        do
        let __s ←
          forIn' [:fvarIds.size] (args, remainingFVarIds) fun i h __s =>
              have args := __s.1;
              have remainingFVarIds := __s.2;
              match Aesop.Substitution.find? { toNat := i } subst with
              | some inst =>
                have args := args.push (some inst);
                pure (ForInStep.yield (args, remainingFVarIds))
              | x =>
                have fvarId := fvarIds[i];
                have args := args.push (some fvarId);
                have remainingFVarIds := remainingFVarIds.push fvarId;
                pure (ForInStep.yield (args, remainingFVarIds))
        have args : Array (Option Lean.Expr) := __s.1
        have remainingFVarIds : Array Lean.Expr := __s.2
        let __do_lift ← Lean.Meta.mkAppOptM' rule args
        Lean.Meta.mkLambdaFVars remainingFVarIds __do_lift

doc:
A representation of the differences between two goals. Each Aesop rule produces
a `GoalDiff` between the goal on which the rule was run (the 'old goal') and
each of the subgoals produced by the rule (the 'new goals').

We use the produced `GoalDiff`s to update stateful data structures which cache
information about Aesop goals and for which it is more efficient to update the
cached information than to recompute it for each goal.

Hypotheses are identified by their `FVarId` *and* type and value (if any).
This means that when a hypothesis `h : T` with `FVarId` `i` appears in the old
goal and `h : T'` with `FVarId` `i` appears in the new goal, but `T` is not
defeq to `T'`, then `h` is treated as both added (with the new type) and
removed (with the old type). This can happen when the type of a hyp changes to
another type that is definitionally equal at `default`, but not at `reducible`
transparency.

The target is identified up to defeq. All defeq comparisons are made at
reducible transparency and metavariables are treated as rigid.

fun diff old new =>
  new.withContext
    (if (diff.oldGoal != old) = true then
      pure
        (some
          (Lean.toMessageData "incorrect old goal: expected " ++ Lean.toMessageData old.name ++
              Lean.toMessageData ", got " ++
            Lean.toMessageData diff.oldGoal.name))
    else
      if (diff.newGoal != new) = true then
        pure
          (some
            (Lean.toMessageData "incorrect new goal: expected " ++ Lean.toMessageData new.name ++
                Lean.toMessageData ", got " ++
              Lean.toMessageData diff.newGoal.name))
      else do
        let __do_lift ← liftM old.getDecl
        have oldLCtx : Lean.LocalContext := __do_lift.lctx
        let __do_lift ← liftM new.getDecl
        have newLCtx : Lean.LocalContext := __do_lift.lctx
        let __s ←
          forIn diff.addedFVars (none, ()) fun fvarId __s =>
              have __do_jp := fun __r =>
                if newLCtx.contains fvarId = true then pure (ForInStep.yield (none, ()))
                else
                  pure
                    (ForInStep.done
                      (some
                          (some
                            (Lean.toMessageData "addedFVars contains hypothesis " ++
                                Lean.toMessageData fvarId.name ++
                              Lean.toMessageData " but this fvar does not exist in the new goal")),
                        ()));
              match oldLCtx.find? fvarId with
              | some oldLDecl => do
                let __do_lift ← liftM fvarId.getDecl
                let __do_lift ← liftM (Aesop.isGoalDiffDefeqLDecl oldLDecl __do_lift)
                if __do_lift = true then
                    pure
                      (ForInStep.done
                        (some
                            (some
                              (Lean.toMessageData "addedFVars contains hypothesis " ++
                                  Lean.toMessageData oldLDecl.userName ++
                                Lean.toMessageData " which was already present in the old goal")),
                          ()))
                  else __do_jp ()
              | x => __do_jp ()
        have __r : Option (Option Lean.MessageData) × Unit := __s
        match __r.1 with
          | some r => pure r
          | none => do
            let __s ←
              forIn diff.removedFVars (none, ()) fun fvarId __s =>
                  have __do_jp := fun __r =>
                    if oldLCtx.contains fvarId = true then pure (ForInStep.yield (none, ()))
                    else
                      pure
                        (ForInStep.done
                          (some
                              (some
                                (Lean.toMessageData "removedFVars contains hypothesis " ++
                                    Lean.toMessageData fvarId.name ++
                                  Lean.toMessageData
                                    " but this fvar does not exist in the old goal")),
                            ()));
                  match newLCtx.find? fvarId with
                  | some newLDecl => do
                    let __do_lift ← liftM fvarId.getDecl
                    let __do_lift ← liftM (Aesop.isGoalDiffDefeqLDecl __do_lift newLDecl)
                    if __do_lift = true then
                        pure
                          (ForInStep.done
                            (some
                                (some
                                  (Lean.toMessageData "removedFVars contains hypothesis " ++
                                      Lean.toMessageData newLDecl.userName ++
                                    Lean.toMessageData " but it is still present in the new goal")),
                              ()))
                      else __do_jp ()
                  | x => __do_jp ()
            have __r : Option (Option Lean.MessageData) × Unit := __s
            match __r.1 with
              | some r => pure r
              | none => do
                let __s ←
                  forIn newLCtx (none, ()) fun newLDecl __s =>
                      if newLDecl.isImplementationDetail = true then
                        pure (ForInStep.yield (none, ()))
                      else
                        have newFVarId := newLDecl.fvarId;
                        if
                            (!oldLCtx.contains newFVarId && !diff.addedFVars.contains newFVarId) =
                              true then
                          pure
                            (ForInStep.done
                              (some
                                  (some
                                    (Lean.toMessageData "hypothesis " ++
                                        Lean.toMessageData newLDecl.userName ++
                                      Lean.toMessageData
                                        " was added, but does not appear in addedFVars")),
                                ()))
                        else pure (ForInStep.yield (none, ()))
                have __r : Option (Option Lean.MessageData) × Unit := __s
                match __r.1 with
                  | some r => pure r
                  | none => do
                    let __s ←
                      forIn oldLCtx (none, ()) fun oldLDecl __s =>
                          if oldLDecl.isImplementationDetail = true then
                            pure (ForInStep.yield (none, ()))
                          else
                            have oldFVarId := oldLDecl.fvarId;
                            if
                                (!newLCtx.contains oldFVarId &&
                                    !diff.removedFVars.contains oldFVarId) =
                                  true then
                              pure
                                (ForInStep.done
                                  (some
                                      (some
                                        (Lean.toMessageData "hypothesis " ++
                                            Lean.toMessageData oldLDecl.userName ++
                                          Lean.toMessageData
                                            " was removed, but does not appear in removedFVars")),
                                    ()))
                            else pure (ForInStep.yield (none, ()))
                    have __r : Option (Option Lean.MessageData) × Unit := __s
                    match __r.1 with
                      | some r => pure r
                      | none => do
                        let __s ←
                          forIn newLCtx (none, ()) fun newLDecl __s =>
                              if newLDecl.isImplementationDetail = true then
                                pure (ForInStep.yield (none, ()))
                              else
                                match oldLCtx.find? newLDecl.fvarId with
                                | some oldLDecl => do
                                  let __do_lift ←
                                    liftM (Aesop.isGoalDiffDefeqLDecl oldLDecl newLDecl)
                                  if __do_lift = true then pure (ForInStep.yield (none, ()))
                                    else
                                      pure
                                        (ForInStep.done
                                          (some
                                              (some
                                                (Lean.toMessageData "hypotheses " ++
                                                        Lean.toMessageData oldLDecl.userName ++
                                                      Lean.toMessageData " and " ++
                                                    Lean.toMessageData newLDecl.userName ++
                                                  Lean.toMessageData
                                                    " have the same FVarId but their types/values are not reducibly defeq")),
                                            ()))
                                | x => pure (ForInStep.yield (none, ()))
                        have __r : Option (Option Lean.MessageData) × Unit := __s
                        match __r.1 with
                          | some r => pure r
                          | none => do
                            let oldTgt ← liftM old.getType
                            let newTgt ← liftM new.getType
                            let __do_lift ←
                              pure diff.targetChanged <&&>
                                  liftM (Aesop.isGoalDiffDefeqExpr oldTgt newTgt)
                            if __do_lift = true then do
                                let oldTgt ←
                                  old.withContext
                                      (Lean.addMessageContext (Lean.toMessageData oldTgt))
                                let newTgt ←
                                  new.withContext
                                      (Lean.addMessageContext (Lean.toMessageData newTgt))
                                pure
                                    (some
                                      (Lean.toMessageData
                                              "diff says target changed, but old target" ++
                                            Lean.toMessageData (Lean.indentD oldTgt) ++
                                          Lean.toMessageData "\nis reducibly defeq to new target" ++
                                        Lean.toMessageData (Lean.indentD newTgt)))
                              else do
                                let __do_lift ←
                                  pure !diff.targetChanged <&&>
                                      notM (liftM (Aesop.isGoalDiffDefeqExpr oldTgt newTgt))
                                if __do_lift = true then do
                                    let oldTgt ←
                                      old.withContext
                                          (Lean.addMessageContext (Lean.toMessageData oldTgt))
                                    let newTgt ←
                                      new.withContext
                                          (Lean.addMessageContext (Lean.toMessageData newTgt))
                                    pure
                                        (some
                                          (Lean.toMessageData
                                                  "diff says target did not change, but old target" ++
                                                Lean.toMessageData (Lean.indentD oldTgt) ++
                                              Lean.toMessageData
                                                "\nis not reducibly defeq to new target" ++
                                            Lean.toMessageData (Lean.indentD newTgt)))
                                  else pure none)

doc:
A rule pattern. For a rule of type `∀ (x₀ : T₀) ... (xₙ : Tₙ), U`, a valid rule
pattern is an expression `p` such that `x₀ : T₁, ..., xₙ : Tₙ ⊢ p : P`. Let
`y₀, ..., yₖ` be those variables `xᵢ` on which `p` depends. When `p` matches an
expression `e`, this means that `e` is defeq to `p` (where each `yᵢ` is replaced
with a metavariable) and we obtain a substitution

    {y₀ ↦ t₀ : T₀, y₁ ↦ t₁ : T₁[x₀ := t₀], ...}

Now suppose we want to match the above rule type against a type `V` (where `V`
is the target for an `apply`-like rule and a hypothesis type for a
`forward`-like rule). To that end, we take `U` and replace each `xᵢ` where
`xᵢ = yⱼ` with `tⱼ` and each `xᵢ` with `xᵢ ≠ yⱼ ∀ j` with a metavariable. The
resulting expression `U'` is then matched against `V`.

        let __do_lift ← liftM (Lean.Meta.isDefEq e p)
        if (!__do_lift) = true then pure none
          else
            have subst := Aesop.Substitution.empty pat.argMap.size pat.levelArgMap.size;

                  have subst := __s;

                    do

doc:
`ParametricAttributeExtra` works around a limitation of `ParametricAttribute`, which is that
definitions must be tagged in the same file that declares the definition.
This works well for definitions in lean core, but for attributes declared outside the core
this is problematic because we may want to tag declarations created before the attribute
was defined.

To resolve this, we allow a one-time exception to the rule that attributes must be applied
in the same file as the declaration: During the declaration of the attribute itself,
we can tag arbitrary other definitions, but once the attribute is declared we must tag things
in the same file as normal.

doc:
Enables the 'unnecessary `<;>`' linter. This will warn whenever the `<;>` tactic combinator
is used when `;` would work.

```
example : True := by apply id <;> trivial
```
The `<;>` is unnecessary here because `apply id` only makes one subgoal.
Prefer `apply id; trivial` instead.

In some cases, the `<;>` is syntactically necessary because a single tactic is expected:
```
example : True := by
  cases () with apply id <;> apply id
  | unit => trivial
```
In this case, you should use parentheses, as in `(apply id; apply id)`:
```
example : True := by
  cases () with (apply id; apply id)
  | unit => trivial
```

                        unused.qsort fun x1 x2 => decide (key x1.1 < key x2.1))
                        last fun x __s =>
                        have last := __s;
                        match x with
                        | (r, stx) =>
                          if
                              (decide (last.start ≤ r.start) && decide (r.stop ≤ last.stop)) =
                                true then
                            pure (ForInStep.yield last)
                          else do
                            Lean.Linter.logLint Batteries.Linter.linter.unnecessarySeqFocus stx
                                ((Lean.MessageData.ofFormat ∘ Std.format)
                                  "Used `tac1 <;> tac2` where `(tac1; tac2)` would suffice")
                            have last : Lean.Syntax.Range := r
                            pure (ForInStep.yield last)
                  pure ()
        else pure (),
  name := `Batteries.Linter.UnnecessarySeqFocus.unnecessarySeqFocusLinter }

doc:
Enables the 'unnecessary `<;>`' linter. This will warn whenever the `<;>` tactic combinator
is used when `;` would work.

```
example : True := by apply id <;> trivial
```
The `<;>` is unnecessary here because `apply id` only makes one subgoal.
Prefer `apply id; trivial` instead.

In some cases, the `<;>` is syntactically necessary because a single tactic is expected:
```
example : True := by
  cases () with apply id <;> apply id
  | unit => trivial
```
In this case, you should use parentheses, as in `(apply id; apply id)`:
```
example : True := by
  cases () with (apply id; apply id)
  | unit => trivial
```

doc:
`tac <;> tac'` runs `tac` on the main goal and `tac'` on each produced goal,
concatenating all goals produced by `tac'`.


Extensions:

 * `t <;> [t1; t2; ...; tn]` focuses on the first goal and applies `t`, which should result in `n`
   subgoals. It then applies each `ti` to the corresponding goal and collects the resulting
   subgoals. It raises an error if the number of subgoals does not match.

doc:
Folds a monadic function over an array from the left, accumulating the partial results starting with
`init`. The accumulated value is combined with the each element of the list in order, using `f`.

The optional parameters `start` and `stop` control the region of the array to be folded. Folding
proceeds from `start` (inclusive) to `stop` (exclusive), so no folding occurs unless `start < stop`.
By default, the entire array is folded.

Examples:
```lean example
example [Monad m] (f : α → β → m α) :
    Array.scanlM f x₀ #[a, b, c] = (do
      let x₁ ← f x₀ a
      let x₂ ← f x₁ b
      let x₃ ← f x₂ c
      pure #[x₀, x₁, x₂, x₃])
    := by simp [scanlM, scanlM.loop]
```

```lean example
example [Monad m] (f : α → β → m α) :
    Array.scanlM f x₀ #[a, b, c] (start := 1) (stop := 3) = (do
      let x₁ ← f x₀ b
      let x₂ ← f x₁ c
      pure #[x₀, x₁, x₂])
    := by simp [scanlM, scanlM.loop]
```

with a rule pattern have exactly one such slot, which is assigned an arbitrary
premise index.

value.text:
fun thm rulePattern? immediate =>
  Lean.Meta.withNewMCtxDepth do
    let __do_lift ← Lean.Meta.inferType thm
    let e ← Lean.instantiateMVars __do_lift
    have numLevelParams : ℕ :=
      (Lean.collectLevelParams { } e).params.size + (Lean.collectLevelMVars { } e).result.size
    let __x ← Lean.Meta.withReducible (Lean.Meta.forallMetaTelescope e)
    match __x with
      | (premises, binderInfos, conclusion) =>
        let premises_1 := Array.map (fun x => x.mvarId!) premises;
        have premiseToIdx := ∅;
        do
        let __s ←
          forIn' [:premises_1.size] premiseToIdx fun i h __s =>
              have premiseToIdx := __s;
              have premiseToIdx := premiseToIdx.insert premises_1[i] { toNat := i };
              pure (ForInStep.yield premiseToIdx)
        have premiseToIdx : Std.HashMap Lean.MVarId Aesop.PremiseIndex := __s
        have slots : Array Aesop.Slot := Array.mkEmpty premises_1.size
        have allDeps : Std.HashSet Aesop.PremiseIndex := ∅
        let __s ←
          forIn' [:premises_1.size] (slots, allDeps) fun i h __s =>
              have slots := __s.1;
              have allDeps := __s.2;
              if
                  (match binderInfos[i]! with
                    | Lean.BinderInfo.instImplicit => true
                    | x => false) =
                    true then
                pure (ForInStep.yield (slots, allDeps))
              else
                have mvarId := premises_1[i];
                do
                let __do_lift ← mvarId.getType
                let typeDiscrTreeKeys ← Aesop.mkDiscrTreePath __do_lift
                have deps : Std.HashSet Aesop.PremiseIndex := ∅
                let __do_lift ← mvarId.getMVarDependencies
                let __s ←
                  forIn __do_lift deps fun dep __s =>
                      have deps := __s;
                      match premiseToIdx[dep]? with
                      | some idx =>
                        have deps := deps.insert idx;
                        pure (ForInStep.yield deps)
                      | x => pure (ForInStep.yield deps)
                have deps : Std.HashSet Aesop.PremiseIndex := __s
                have slots : Array Aesop.Slot :=
                  slots.push
                    { typeDiscrTreeKeys? := some typeDiscrTreeKeys, index := default,
                      premiseIndex := { toNat := i }, deps := deps, common := default,
                      forwardDeps := default }
                have allDeps : Std.HashSet Aesop.PremiseIndex := allDeps.insertMany deps
                pure (ForInStep.yield (slots, allDeps))
        have slots : Array Aesop.Slot := __s.1
        have allDeps : Std.HashSet Aesop.PremiseIndex := __s.2
        have patBoundPremises : Std.HashSet Aesop.PremiseIndex :=
          (Option.map
                (fun x => Std.HashSet.ofArray (Array.map (fun x => { toNat := x }) x.boundPremises))
                rulePattern?).getD
            ∅
        have slots : Array Aesop.Slot :=
          Array.filter
            (fun s =>
              have idx := s.premiseIndex;
              !allDeps.contains idx && !patBoundPremises.contains idx &&
                Aesop.UnorderedArraySet.contains idx immediate)
            slots
        have __do_jp : Unit → Array Aesop.Slot → Lean.MetaM Aesop.ForwardRuleInfo :=
          fun __r slots =>
          have slotClusters :=
            Array.map Aesop.ForwardRuleInfo.ofExpr.sortSlots✝
              (Aesop.cluster (fun x => x.deps.toArray) slots);
          if
              (!slotClusters.any fun cluster =>
                    cluster.any fun slot => decide (slot.index.toNat > 0) && slot.common.isEmpty) =
                true then
            do
            let __do_lift ← Lean.Meta.getMVars conclusion
            have conclusionDeps : Array Aesop.PremiseIndex :=
              Array.filterMap (fun x => premiseToIdx[x]?) __do_lift
            have rulePatternInfo? : Option (Aesop.RulePattern × Aesop.PremiseIndex) :=
              Option.map (fun x => (x, { toNat := premises_1.size })) rulePattern?
            pure
                { numPremises := premises_1.size, numLevelParams := numLevelParams,
                  slotClusters := slotClusters, conclusionDeps := conclusionDeps,
                  rulePatternInfo? := rulePatternInfo? }
          else
            panicWithPosWithDecl "Aesop.Forward.RuleInfo" "Aesop.ForwardRuleInfo.ofExpr" 144 2
              ("assertion violation: " ++
                "! slotClusters.any λ cluster => cluster.any λ slot =>\n    slot.index.toNat > 0 && slot.common.isEmpty\n  ")
        if rulePattern?.isSome = true then
            have slots :=
              slots.push
                { typeDiscrTreeKeys? := none, index := default,
                  premiseIndex := { toNat := premises_1.size }, deps := patBoundPremises,
                  common := default, forwardDeps := default };
            __do_jp () slots
          else __do_jp () slots

doc:
Two matches are equivalent if (a) they have the same level; (b) for each
premise that appears in a slot greater than the matches' level, their
substitution assigns the same value; (c) for each premise that appears in the
rule's conclusion, their substitution assigns the same value.

If we already have a match `m₁` and we obtain an equivalent match `m₂`, then
`m₂` is redundant. This is because if the matches are partial, then `m₂` can be
completed by exactly the hypotheses that complete `m₁`, since they agree on the
premise instantiations that are relevant for the possible completions. And if
the matches are complete, then they assign the same instantiations to the
variables that appear in the rule's conclusion, and these are the only ones that
ultimately matter.

value.text:
fun m₁ m₂ =>
  (m₁.level == m₂.level &&
      m₁.forwardDeps.all fun p =>
        Aesop.Substitution.find? p m₁.subst == Aesop.Substitution.find? p m₂.subst) &&
    m₁.conclusionDeps.all fun p =>
      Aesop.Substitution.find? p m₁.subst == Aesop.Substitution.find? p m₂.subst

doc:
Constructs the hypotheses for the structure extensionality theorem that
states that two structures are equal if their fields are equal.

Calls the continuation `k` with the list of parameters to the structure,
two structure variables `x` and `y`, and a list of pairs `(field, ty)`
where each `ty` is of the form `x.field = y.field` or `x.field ≍ y.field`.

If `flat` parses to `true`, any fields inherited from parent structures
are treated as fields of the given structure type.
If it is `false`, then the behind-the-scenes encoding of inherited fields
is visible in the extensionality lemma.

fun {α} struct flat k => do
  let __do_lift ← Lean.getEnv
  have __do_jp : Unit → Lean.MetaM α := fun __r => do
    let structC ← Lean.mkConstWithLevelParams struct
    let __do_lift ← Lean.Meta.inferType structC
    Lean.Meta.forallTelescope __do_lift fun params x =>
        Lean.Meta.withImplicitBinderInfos params
          (Lean.Meta.withLocalDecl `x Lean.BinderInfo.implicit (Lean.mkAppN structC params) fun x =>
            Lean.Meta.withLocalDecl `y Lean.BinderInfo.implicit (Lean.mkAppN structC params)
              fun y =>
              have hyps := #[];
              have __do_jp := fun fields => do
                let __s ←
                  forIn fields hyps fun field __s =>
                      have hyps := __s;
                      do
                      let x_f ← Lean.Meta.mkProjection x field
                      let y_f ← Lean.Meta.mkProjection y field
                      let __do_lift ← Lean.Meta.isProof x_f
                      if __do_lift = true then pure (ForInStep.yield hyps)
                        else do
                          let __do_lift ← Lean.Meta.mkEqHEq x_f y_f
                          have hyps : Array (Lean.Name × Lean.Expr) := hyps.push (field, __do_lift)
                          pure (ForInStep.yield hyps)
                have hyps : Array (Lean.Name × Lean.Expr) := __s
                k params x y hyps;
              if flat = true then do
                let __do_lift ← Lean.getEnv
                let fields ← pure (Lean.getStructureFieldsFlattened __do_lift struct false)
                __do_jp fields
              else do
                let __do_lift ← Lean.getEnv
                let fields ← pure (Lean.getStructureFields __do_lift struct)
                __do_jp fields)
  if Lean.isStructure __do_lift struct = true then __do_jp ()
    else do
      let __r ←
        Lean.throwError
            (Lean.toMessageData "Internal error when constructing `ext` hypotheses: `" ++
                Lean.toMessageData struct ++
              Lean.toMessageData "` is not a structure")
      __do_jp __r

fun extThmName =>
  Lean.Meta.withLCtx { } ∅ do
    let __do_lift ← Lean.getConstInfo extThmName
    Lean.Meta.forallTelescopeReducing __do_lift.type fun args ty =>
        have failNotEq :=
          Lean.throwError
            (Lean.toMessageData
                    "Expected a theorem proving a proposition of the form `x = y`, but `" ++
                  Lean.toMessageData (Lean.MessageData.ofConstName extThmName) ++
                Lean.toMessageData "` proves" ++
              Lean.toMessageData (Lean.indentD (Lean.MessageData.ofExpr ty)));
        match ty.eq? with
        | some (fst, x, y) =>
          match Array.findIdx? (fun x_1 => x_1 == x) args with
          | some xIdx =>
            match Array.findIdx? (fun x => x == y) args with
            | some yIdx =>
              have __do_jp := fun __r =>
                have startIdx := yIdx + 1;
                have toRevert := Std.Slice.toArray (Std.Rci.Sliceable.mkSlice args startIdx...*);
                do
                let fvars ←
                  Array.foldlM
                      (fun st e => do
                        let __do_lift ← Lean.Meta.inferType e
                        pure (Lean.collectFVars st __do_lift))
                      { } toRevert
                forIn toRevert PUnit.unit fun fvar __s => do
                    let __do_lift ← Lean.Meta.isProof fvar
                    have __do_jp : Unit → Lean.MetaM (ForInStep PUnit.{1}) := fun __r =>
                      if Std.TreeSet.contains fvars.fvarSet fvar.fvarId! = true then do
                        Lean.throwError
                            (Lean.toMessageData "Argument `" ++ Lean.toMessageData fvar ++
                                      Lean.toMessageData
                                        "` is depended upon by a subsequent argument, which is not supported for arguments after `" ++
                                    Lean.toMessageData x ++
                                  Lean.toMessageData "` and `" ++
                                Lean.toMessageData y ++
                              Lean.toMessageData "`")
                        pure (ForInStep.yield PUnit.unit)
                      else pure (ForInStep.yield PUnit.unit)
                    if __do_lift = true then __do_jp ()
                      else do
                        let __r ←
                          Lean.throwError
                              (Lean.toMessageData "Argument `" ++ Lean.toMessageData fvar ++
                                        Lean.toMessageData
                                          "` is not a proof, but all arguments after `" ++
                                      Lean.toMessageData x ++
                                    Lean.toMessageData "` and `" ++
                                  Lean.toMessageData y ++
                                Lean.toMessageData "` must be proofs")
                        __do_jp __r
                let __do_lift ← Array.mapM (fun x => Lean.Meta.inferType x) toRevert
                have conj : Lean.Expr := Lean.mkAndN __do_lift.toList
                have newBis : Array (Lean.FVarId × Lean.BinderInfo) := #[]
                let __s ←
                  forIn (Std.Rio.Sliceable.mkSlice args *...startIdx) newBis fun fvar __s =>
                      have newBis := __s;
                      do
                      let __do_lift ← fvar.fvarId!.getBinderInfo
                      if
                            (match __do_lift with
                              | Lean.BinderInfo.default => true
                              | Lean.BinderInfo.strictImplicit => true
                              | x => false) =
                              true then
                          have newBis := newBis.push (fvar.fvarId!, Lean.BinderInfo.implicit);
                          pure (ForInStep.yield newBis)
                        else pure (ForInStep.yield newBis)
                have newBis : Array (Lean.FVarId × Lean.BinderInfo) := __s
                Lean.Meta.withNewBinderInfos newBis
                    (Lean.Meta.mkForallFVars (↑(Std.Rio.Sliceable.mkSlice args *...startIdx))
                      (Lean.mkIff ty conj));
              if (xIdx + 1 == yIdx) = true then __do_jp ()
              else do
                let __r ←
                  Lean.throwError
                      (Lean.toMessageData "Expected `" ++ Lean.toMessageData x ++
                            Lean.toMessageData "` and `" ++
                          Lean.toMessageData y ++
                        Lean.toMessageData "` to be consecutive arguments")
                __do_jp __r
            | x => failNotEq
          | x => failNotEq
        | x => failNotEq

fun goal =>

    let tgt ← goal.getType'
    have __do_jp : Unit → Lean.MetaM (List Lean.MVarId) := fun __r =>
      have ty := tgt.getArg! 0;
      do
      let s ← Lean.saveState
      let __do_lift ← Lean.Meta.Ext.getExtTheorems ty
      let __s ←
        forIn __do_lift (none, ()) fun lem __s => do
            let e ←
              tryCatch
                  (do
                    Lean.Meta.withNewMCtxDepth do
                        let c ← Lean.Meta.mkConstWithFreshMVarLevels lem.declName
                        let __do_lift ← Lean.Meta.inferType c
                        let __x ←
                          Lean.Meta.withDefault (Lean.Meta.forallMetaTelescopeReducing __do_lift)
                        match __x with
                          | (fst, fst_1, declTy) => do
                            let __do_lift ← Lean.Meta.isDefEq tgt declTy
                            guard (__do_lift = true)
                    let __do_lift ← Lean.Meta.mkConstWithFreshMVarLevels lem.declName
                    let __do_lift ← goal.apply __do_lift { newGoals := Lean.Meta.ApplyNewGoals.all }
                    EarlyReturnT.return __do_lift)
                  fun x => do
                  let __r ← s.restore
                  ExceptT.run (pure __r)
            EarlyReturn.runK e (fun r => pure (ForInStep.done (some r, ()))) fun __r =>
                pure (ForInStep.yield (none, ()))
      have __r : Option (List Lean.MVarId) × Unit := __s
      match __r.1 with
        | some r => pure r
        | none =>
          Lean.throwError
            (Lean.toMessageData "No applicable extensionality theorem found for type" ++
                Lean.toMessageData (Lean.indentExpr ty) ++
              (Lean.toMessageData
                  "Extensionality theorems can be registered by marking them with the `[ext]` attribute").note)
    if tgt.isAppOfArity `Eq 3 = true then __do_jp ()
      else do
        let __r ←
          Lean.throwError
              (Lean.toMessageData "This extensionality tactic only applies to equalities, not" ++
                Lean.toMessageData (Lean.indentExpr tgt))
        __do_jp __r

doc:
This method makes sure each discriminant is a free variable.
Return the tuple `(discrsNew, discrEqs, mvarId)`. `discrsNew` in an array representing the new discriminants, `discrEqs` is an array of auxiliary equality hypotheses
that connect the new discriminants to the original terms they represent.
Remark: `discrEqs.size ≤ discrsNew.size`

Remark:
  We should only generalize `discrs` occurrences as `match`-expression discriminants.
  For example, given the following goal.
  ```
  x : Nat
  ⊢ (match g x with
      | 0 => 1
      | Nat.succ y => g x) =
      2 * x + 1
  ```
  we should not generalize the `g x` in the rhs of the second alternative, and the two resulting goals
  for the `split` tactic  should be
  ```
  case h_1
  x x✝ : Nat
  h✝ : g x = 0
  ⊢ 1 = 2 * x + 1

  case h_2
  x x✝ y✝ : Nat
  h✝ : g x = Nat.succ y✝
  ⊢ g x = 2 * x + 1
  ```

Split works best if all discriminants are already free variables. If they are not, it will generalize
them, but that may fail if the motive is dependent. So to avoid that, we first generalize all
non-FVar discriminants that are propositions; because of proof irrelevance, that's much simpler.

to the match to the local context. Returns the new goal, the added hypothesis
and the hypotheses that were removed (if any). Hypotheses may be removed if the
match is for a `destruct` rule. If `skipExistingProps` is `true`, propositional

    (pure (Lean.toMessageData "apply complete match"))

      let name ← Lean.Meta.getUnusedUserName Aesop.forwardHypPrefix
      let __x ← liftM (Aesop.ForwardRuleMatch.getProof goal m)
      match __x with
        | some prf => do
          let type ← liftM (Lean.Meta.inferType prf)
          have __do_jp :
            Unit →
              Aesop.ScriptT Aesop.BaseM (Option (Lean.MVarId × Lean.FVarId × Array Lean.FVarId)) :=
            fun __r =>
            have hyp := { userName := name, type := type, value := prf };

            let __x ← Aesop.assertHypothesisS goal hyp Lean.Meta.TransparencyMode.default

              | (goal, #[hyp]) =>
                if (!m.rule.destruct) = true then pure (some (goal, hyp, #[]))

                    (pure (Lean.toMessageData "check whether hyp already exists")) do
                    let result ← liftM (Aesop.isHypRedundantReducibleRigid type)
                    let __do_lift ← Aesop.TraceOption.forwardDebug.isEnabled
                    have __do_jp : Unit → Aesop.ScriptT Aesop.BaseM Bool := fun __r => pure result
                    if __do_lift = true then do

                              (Lean.toMessageData "already exists: " ++ Lean.toMessageData result)

            else __do_jp ()

fun {m} [Monad m] [MonadLiftT Lean.MetaM m] {α β} e f map => do
  let lctx ←
    have this := Lean.getLCtx;
      liftM this
  have rep : Lean.PArray (Option (Lean.Expr × α)) := map.rep
  let __do_lift ← Aesop.EMap.getCandidates✝ e map
  let __s ←
    forIn __do_lift (none, rep) fun i __s =>
        have rep := __s.2;
        match map.rep[i]! with
        | some (e', old) =>
          if (e'.hasAnyFVar fun x => !lctx.contains x) = true then
            have rep := Lean.PersistentArray.set rep i none;
            pure (ForInStep.yield (none, rep))
          else do
            let __do_lift ← liftM (Aesop.isDefEqReducibleRigid e' e)
            if __do_lift = true then do
                let __x ← f old
                match __x with
                  | (new?, b) =>
                    have entry := Option.map (fun x => (e', x)) new?;
                    pure
                      (ForInStep.done
                        (some
                            ({ rep := Lean.PersistentArray.set rep i entry, idx := map.idx },
                              some b),
                          rep))
              else pure (ForInStep.yield (none, rep))
        | x => pure (ForInStep.yield (none, rep))
  have __r : Option (Aesop.EMap α × Option β) := __s.1
  have rep : Lean.PArray (Option (Lean.Expr × α)) := __s.2
  match __r with
    | some r => pure r
    | none => pure ({ rep := rep, idx := map.idx }, none)

must be a valid index).

fun premises lmvarIds cs slot hyp =>
  match cs.slots[slot.toNat]? with
  | some slot =>
    have premiseIdx := slot.premiseIndex.toNat;
    match premises[premiseIdx]? with
    | some slotPremise => do
      let premiseType ← liftM slotPremise.getType
      let hypType ← liftM hyp.getType
      Aesop.withAesopTraceNodeBefore Aesop.TraceOption.forward
          (pure
            (Lean.toMessageData "match against premise " ++ Lean.toMessageData premiseIdx ++
                    Lean.toMessageData ": " ++
                  Lean.toMessageData hypType ++
                Lean.toMessageData " ≟ " ++
              Lean.toMessageData premiseType))
          (Lean.withoutModifyingState do
            let isDefEq ←
              Aesop.withConstAesopTraceNode Aesop.TraceOption.forwardDebug
                  (pure (Lean.toMessageData "defeq check"))
                  (Lean.Meta.withReducible (liftM (Lean.Meta.isDefEq premiseType hypType)))
            if isDefEq = true then
                have subst := Aesop.Substitution.empty premises.size lmvarIds.size;
                do
                let __s ←
                  forIn slot.deps subst fun var __s =>
                      have subst := __s;
                      do
                      let subst ←
                        Aesop.ClusterState.matchPremise?.updateSubst✝ hyp premises var subst
                      pure (ForInStep.yield subst)
                have subst : Aesop.Substitution := __s
                have subst : Aesop.Substitution :=
                  Aesop.Substitution.insert slot.premiseIndex (Lean.Expr.fvar hyp) subst
                let __s ←
                  forIn' [:lmvarIds.size] subst fun i h __s =>
                      have subst := __s;
                      do
                      let __do_lift ← Lean.getLevelMVarAssignment? lmvarIds[i]
                      match __do_lift with
                        | some l => do
                          let __do_lift ← Lean.instantiateLevelMVars l
                          have subst : Aesop.Substitution :=
                            Aesop.Substitution.insertLevel { toNat := i } __do_lift subst
                          pure (ForInStep.yield subst)
                        | x => pure (ForInStep.yield subst)
                have subst : Aesop.Substitution := __s
                let __do_lift ← Aesop.TraceOption.forward.isEnabled
                have __do_jp : Unit → Aesop.BaseM (Option Aesop.Substitution) := fun __r =>
                  pure (some subst)
                if __do_lift = true then do
                    let __r ←
                      Lean.addTrace Aesop.TraceOption.forward.traceClass
                          (Lean.toMessageData "substitution: " ++ Lean.toMessageData subst)
                    __do_jp __r
                  else __do_jp ()
              else pure none)
    | x =>
      Lean.throwError
        (Lean.toMessageData "aesop: internal error: matchPremise?: slot with premise index " ++
                Lean.toMessageData premiseIdx ++
              Lean.toMessageData ", but only " ++
            Lean.toMessageData premises.size ++
          Lean.toMessageData " premises")
  | x =>
    Lean.throwError
      (Lean.toMessageData "aesop: internal error: matchPremise?: no slot with index " ++
        Lean.toMessageData slot)

doc:
A goal `G` can be added to the tree for three reasons:

1. `G` was produced by its parent rule as a subgoal. This is the most common
   reason.
2. `G` was copied because it contains some metavariables which were assigned by
   its parent rule. In this case, we record goal of which `G` is a copy. We also
   record the representative of the equivalence class of goals which are copies
   of each other. E.g. if goal `1` is copied to goal `2` and goal `2` is copied
   to goal `3`, they are all part of the equivalence class with representative
   `1`.
